The firewall log shows two matches per request, one Warning at score 3 from a protocol rule and one Error at score 4 on the notes field, and the policy runs in prevention mode. Clinics are queueing. What do you do right now?
options: Add a per-rule exclusion for the notes field on the specific rule that is matching, using the request attribute values variable
Switch the whole WAF policy to detection mode until the rule set can be retuned this evening
Raise the anomaly score threshold above 7 on the policy so two matches no longer add up to a block
Add a custom rule with priority 1 that allows any request whose URI path is the appointment-notes endpoint
cards.answer: Add a per-rule exclusion for the notes field on the specific rule that is matching, using the request attribute values variable
cards.why: Anomaly scoring blocks at a total of 5, so a Warning at 3 plus an Error at 4 crosses the threshold even though neither would alone; the surgical containment is an exclusion narrowed to the offending request attribute and rule, which Microsoft explicitly recommends over broader exclusions. The nearest wrong option is the custom rule with an Allow action, which would work and is tempting under pressure, but an Allow short-circuits all lower-priority evaluation so the entire notes endpoint stops being inspected for SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Switching the policy to detection mode disarms the WAF for every site behind it, and the anomaly threshold of 5 is not a customer-tunable dial.
cards.citation: Azure Web Application Firewall on Application Gateway and Web Application Firewall exclusion lists · outline 3.3

cards.q: A logistics company's AKS cluster is alerting. Defender for Cloud has raised a digital currency mining alert on a pod in the tracking namespace, and node CPU is pinned. The Defender sensor is deployed and the Azure Policy add-on is installed. The image itself is clean in the registry, so the miner binary arrived at runtime. Engineering needs the process stopped on every affected node in the next few minutes, without deleting the namespace.
options: Configure a binary drift policy in Defender for Containers with blocking, so unauthorized external processes are stopped inside the containers
Set the data plane hardening policy that restricts containers to allowed images only to a Deny effect so the miner cannot be scheduled again
Apply a Kubernetes network policy denying egress from the tracking namespace so the miner cannot reach its pool
Enable agentless scanning for machines so the node disk snapshot identifies the dropped binary for removal
cards.answer: Configure a binary drift policy in Defender for Containers with blocking, so unauthorized external processes are stopped inside the containers
cards.why: Binary drift is the sensor-based capability aimed exactly at processes that were not in the image, and it has both a detection mode and a blocking mode where you define drift policies specifying the conditions under which processes are blocked. That is the only option that stops the running process. The nearest wrong option is the network policy: cutting egress is a reasonable parallel action and would degrade the miner's usefulness, but the process keeps consuming the nodes and the pod stays compromised. The allowed-images recommendation is admission control, so its Deny effect governs the next scheduling decision rather than the container already running.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Containers introduction, binary drift protection · outline 3.3

cards.q: A challenger bank's API Management gateway is under a credential-stuffing wave. The sign-in operation is taking roughly forty thousand calls an hour from thousands of residential addresses, each address low and slow, and the backend identity service is browning out. The API already validates Microsoft Entra tokens on other operations, but sign-in is by definition open to anonymous callers. Product will not accept blocking whole countries.
options: Apply a rate-limit-by-key policy scoped to the sign-in operation with a counter key derived from the caller address and a short renewal period
Apply a quota-by-key policy on the sign-in operation to cap the number of calls each caller may make this month
Apply an ip-filter policy in the inbound section with an allow action listing the known corporate address ranges
Apply a validate-jwt policy to the sign-in operation with require-expiration-time and require-signed-tokens set to true
cards.answer: Apply a rate-limit-by-key policy scoped to the sign-in operation with a counter key derived from the caller address and a short renewal period
cards.why: Microsoft's OWASP API guidance names rate limiting as the mitigation that blunts brute-force and credential-stuffing pressure, and recommends stricter limits on sensitive endpoints such as sign-in and password reset; rate-limit-by-key throttles per key over a sliding window of up to 300 seconds and returns 429 to callers who exceed it. The nearest wrong option is quota-by-key, which is a real and related policy but is designed for long time frames and total consumption budgeting, so it neither reacts within the hour nor protects the backend from a burst. An allow-action ip-filter would lock out every legitimate retail customer, and validate-jwt cannot help on an endpoint whose whole job is to issue credentials to anonymous callers.
cards.citation: API Management mitigations for OWASP API threats, rate-limit-by-key policy reference · outline 3.3

cards.q: A secret-scanning alert fires against a public GitHub fork belonging to a contractor at an energy utility. The leaked value is a function app master key, and the commit is two days old. Access logs show calls to the app's admin path from an address outside the utility's ranges. The function app fronts meter-reading ingestion and cannot be taken offline during the settlement window.
options: Renew the master key immediately, then set the site property that isolates the administrative endpoints so the runtime REST APIs stop answering
Renew every function key on the app, since function keys take precedence over host keys and will override the leaked master key
Change the app's secret storage type to keyvault, which invalidates the previously issued keys as part of the migration
Add an access restriction rule denying the attacker address, then rotate the master key at the end of the settlement window
cards.answer: Renew the master key immediately, then set the site property that isolates the administrative endpoints so the runtime REST APIs stop answering
cards.why: The master key is a host key with administrative reach over the runtime REST APIs under the admin path, so renewal is the only thing that revokes the attacker's access, and Functions supports disabling administrative endpoints through the functionsRuntimeAdminIsolationEnabled site property, which removes the attack surface rather than just the credential. The nearest wrong option is rotating function keys: precedence between function and host keys only decides which key is used when two share a name, and it does nothing to invalidate _master. Blocking one address defers the rotation while the key is still valid and published, and changing the secret storage location moves where keys live without revoking their values.
cards.citation: Work with access keys in Azure Functions and Securing Azure Functions · outline 3.3

cards.q: After a quarter of incidents, an insurer reviews how its public APIs are fronted. Today, API Management sits directly on the internet with subscription keys on every product and token validation on most operations. Two of the incidents were volumetric layer 7 floods and one was a scanner walking undocumented paths. The architecture board asks what should have been in place before any of it started.
options: A web application firewall on Application Gateway or Front Door deployed upstream of the gateway, with the Bot Manager rule set enabled
A second API Management instance in a paired region so flood traffic can be shed across gateways
Client certificate authentication on every product, replacing subscription keys as the primary caller control
Private endpoints on the API Management gateway so all callers reach it over Private Link
cards.answer: A web application firewall on Application Gateway or Front Door deployed upstream of the gateway, with the Bot Manager rule set enabled
cards.why: Microsoft's API Management guidance is explicit that for defence in depth a WAF should be deployed upstream of the instance, using Application Gateway or Front Door, and its resource-consumption recommendations point at bot protection with the Microsoft bot manager rule set in front of the gateway for layer 7 pressure. The nearest wrong option is private endpoints, which is genuinely recommended for hiding internal API endpoints from the internet, but these are public consumer APIs that must stay reachable, so Private Link solves a different problem. Client certificates strengthen caller identity yet do nothing about volumetric floods, and a second region adds capacity rather than inspection.
cards.citation: Azure API Management API authentication and authorization, plus OWASP API threat mitigations · outline 3.3

cards.q: A pharmaceutical manufacturer spends a quiet week hardening its container supply chain. Images are built in a pipeline, pushed to a Premium Azure Container Registry, and pulled by four AKS clusters. Two clusters were found running images sideloaded from a public registry during an outage last year. The registry still has Docker Content Trust enabled from an old project, and the security lead asks how signing and provenance should look going forward.
options: Adopt Notary Project signing and verification, and enforce the trusted-registries data plane hardening policy on every cluster
Keep Docker Content Trust as the signing standard and extend it to the remaining repositories, since it is already enabled on this Premium registry
Rely on Defender for Containers registry vulnerability assessment, since a signed findings artifact is attached to each scanned image
Enable the AKS image cleaner on each cluster so images that did not come from the approved registry are removed automatically
cards.answer: Adopt Notary Project signing and verification, and enforce the trusted-registries data plane hardening policy on every cluster
cards.why: AKS registry-security guidance names image signing and verification with the Notary Project as the way to prove provenance, and Kubernetes data plane hardening includes a recommendation that container images be deployed from trusted registries only, which is one of the recommendations requiring you to configure the registry list as a policy parameter and can be moved from audit to Deny. Docker Content Trust is the nearest wrong option precisely because it is already on: Microsoft has closed it to new registries as of May 2026 and is removing it entirely in March 2028, with a documented transition to Notary. The Defender vulnerability findings artifact is signed by Microsoft for the integrity of the findings themselves and is not an image provenance control, and image cleaner removes unused vulnerable images rather than enforcing origin.
cards.citation: Security concepts for applications and clusters in AKS, Kubernetes data plane hardening, and Docker Content Trust in Azure Container Registry · outline 3.3

cards.q: A grocery retailer has Defender for Cloud switched on across 40 Azure subscriptions and is working the Recommendations page by hand. The lead analyst notices the risk level and attack path columns are greyed out and unusable, so nobody can tell which of 900 open recommendations actually matters. Finance will fund exactly one change. What do you buy?
options: Turn on the paid Defender CSPM plan on the subscriptions
Turn on Defender for Servers Plan 2 on the subscriptions
Assign the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark to each subscription
Configure continuous export of recommendations to a Log Analytics workspace
cards.answer: Turn on the paid Defender CSPM plan on the subscriptions
cards.why: Risk prioritization, attack path analysis and governance are capabilities of the paid Defender CSPM plan; without it those columns render blurred in the recommendations experience. Defender for Servers Plan 2 is the nearest miss because it does bring agentless machine scanning and vulnerability findings, but it is a workload protection plan and does not unlock risk-based ranking of recommendations. MCSB is already applied by default the moment Defender for Cloud is enabled, so assigning it changes nothing.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, What is Cloud Security Posture Management and Risk prioritization · outline 4.1

cards.q: A teaching hospital runs Defender CSPM with agentless scanning enabled. The CISO asks a very specific question before the board meeting: which internet-facing virtual machines carry a managed identity that can reach a storage account holding patient records? No pre-built page answers exactly that. Where do you go?
options: Build a graph query in Cloud security explorer
Open the Attack path analysis page and read the listed paths
Filter the Inventory page by internet exposure and export the CSV
Write a Kusto query in Azure Resource Graph Explorer against securityresources
cards.answer: Build a graph query in Cloud security explorer
cards.why: Cloud security explorer lets you run your own path-finding queries over the cloud security graph, correlating exposure, identity permissions, and data sensitivity in one question. Attack path analysis is the closest wrong answer: it surfaces only the exploitable paths the proprietary algorithm has already computed and ranked, so it cannot be steered at an arbitrary ad hoc correlation. Resource Graph reaches asset and assessment records but not the graph relationships between identity, exposure and data.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Security explorer and attack paths · outline 4.1

cards.q: A retail bank passes its card audit on Azure but the assessor now wants the same evidence for the AWS accounts that run the loyalty platform. Only Foundational CSPM is on in AWS today. The security architect must get PCI DSS v4.0.1 results showing for those accounts. What is the correct sequence?
options: Enable a paid Defender plan on the AWS accounts, then switch PCI DSS v4.0.1 on through Manage compliance policies at the AWS management account scope
Create an assessment for PCI DSS in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager and point it at the AWS connector
Assign the built-in PCI DSS Azure Policy initiative to the Azure management group that holds the AWS security connector resources
Author a custom recommendation set in Defender for Cloud that mirrors the PCI DSS controls for AWS
cards.answer: Enable a paid Defender plan on the AWS accounts, then switch PCI DSS v4.0.1 on through Manage compliance policies at the AWS management account scope
cards.why: Standards beyond the defaults can only be added once at least one paid plan is on for the scope, and they are assigned from Manage compliance policies against the account or management account; Microsoft advises picking the highest applicable scope so nested resources aggregate. Assigning the Azure Policy initiative is the tempting near miss, because Azure standards do ride on policy initiatives, but that path assesses Azure resources and will not evaluate AWS resources reached through the connector. Compliance Manager consumes the resulting data rather than producing it.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Assign regulatory compliance standards and Regulatory compliance standards · outline 4.1

cards.q: A university has ISO IEC 27001:2022 assigned in Defender for Cloud. One control sits permanently grey with no pass or fail, because it covers a background-screening process that no cloud signal can observe. The auditor arrives in three weeks and wants that control evidenced. What does the security team do in the dashboard?
options: Open the control, attest against the manual assessment and attach the supporting evidence
Create an exemption for the control so it stops counting against the standard
Create a disable rule so the control no longer appears in the standard
Wait for the next assessment cycle, since assessments refresh roughly every twelve hours
cards.answer: Open the control, attest against the manual assessment and attach the supporting evidence
cards.why: Standards mix automated and manual assessments; manual ones are cleared by selecting the assessment, choosing the subscriptions, selecting Attest and attaching evidence, which is exactly the audit artefact wanted. An exemption is the plausible wrong turn, since it also removes a red mark, but it records that a requirement is being skipped rather than demonstrating it is met. Waiting achieves nothing because a control with no automatable signal never resolves itself, and disable rules belong to vulnerability findings, not compliance controls.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Improve regulatory compliance · outline 4.1

cards.q: A car parts manufacturer has 600 machines in one subscription. Only the 80 machines in the plant network are in budget for protection this year, and the requirement is endpoint detection and response on those 80 and nothing else. The machines already carry an ownership tag. What deployment does the engineer choose?
options: Enable Defender for Servers Plan 1 at the resource level for the tagged machines using the granular pricing policy
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 2 at the resource level for the tagged machines using the granular pricing policy
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 2 on the subscription and add the other 520 machines as agentless scanning exclusion tags
Enable Defender CSPM on the subscription and rely on agentless machine scanning for the plant machines
cards.answer: Enable Defender for Servers Plan 1 at the resource level for the tagged machines using the granular pricing policy
cards.why: Plan 1 is the entry-level tier built around the Defender for Endpoint integration and it is the only Servers plan that can be enabled at resource level, which the Security Center granular pricing policy definitions do by tag. Plan 2 at resource level is the trap: Plan 2 can only be disabled per resource, never enabled per resource, so that assignment cannot exist. Exclusion tags on agentless scanning only skip scanning, they do not stop the subscription from being billed or protected, and CSPM alone brings posture scanning rather than endpoint detection and response.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Select a Defender for Servers plan and Protect your servers with Defender for Servers · outline 4.1

cards.q: A fashion retailer creates storage accounts constantly as new brand microsites launch, and two of them went live last quarter with no threat protection at all. The security team wants every existing and future storage account under a management group protected on the same settings, without chasing each subscription owner. Which enablement method fits?
options: Enable Defender for Storage with the Azure built-in policy scoped to the management group
Enable Defender for Storage from the Environment settings page of each subscription
Create a workflow automation that triggers a Logic App whenever a new storage account appears
Enable Defender CSPM so that sensitive data discovery covers the new storage accounts
cards.answer: Enable Defender for Storage with the Azure built-in policy scoped to the management group
cards.why: Microsoft recommends policy-based enablement precisely for this case: it applies one consistent configuration across every current and future storage account inside the scope, including whole management groups. Toggling each subscription in the portal is the near miss, because it does protect accounts that exist now, but nothing carries the setting to subscriptions or accounts created later. Workflow automation reacts after the fact and Defender CSPM gives posture and data discovery, not the storage threat detection and malware scanning of the workload plan.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Deploy Microsoft Defender for Storage · outline 4.1

cards.q: A payments firm runs AWS Organizations with 60 member accounts and creates new ones most months. Security operations centralised administration into a dedicated security account long ago and wants Defender for Cloud posture on every account, including future ones, without a manual onboarding ritual each time. How is the connector built?
options: Create one connector from the AWS management account with Onboard set to Management account, then deploy the template as both a Stack and a StackSet
Create one connector from the delegated administrator security account with Onboard set to Management account
Create a Single account connector for each existing member account and repeat the process for each new account
Connect the organization to Microsoft Sentinel first, then let Defender for Cloud inherit those accounts
cards.answer: Create one connector from the AWS management account with Onboard set to Management account, then deploy the template as both a Stack and a StackSet
cards.why: Management account onboarding auto-provisions connectors for discovered member accounts and for accounts created later, and when onboarding a management account the CloudFormation template must be run as a Stack and as a StackSet, with AWS Organizations trusted access enabled. Using the delegated administrator account is the seductive wrong answer because it matches normal AWS practice, but Defender for Cloud explicitly does not support delegated administrator accounts for this. An account already wired to Microsoft Sentinel needs the separate documented procedure rather than inheriting anything.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Defender for Cloud docs, connect an AWS account · outline 4.1

cards.q: A broadcaster is onboarding a GCP organization. The Google platform team asks the Azure engineer which downloadable service account key to send over, and how often it should be rotated. What does the engineer tell them, and what does the onboarding actually require on the GCP side?
options: No key is issued; the generated gcloud script creates a workload identity pool, a provider per plan and service accounts, and the required Google APIs must be enabled on the project running the script
A service account JSON key is generated in GCP and pasted into the connector wizard, then rotated every 90 days
An Azure Arc agent is installed on every compute instance first, and that agent identity is what Defender for Cloud authenticates with
A CloudFormation-equivalent Deployment Manager template is uploaded to a Cloud Storage bucket and referenced by URL
cards.answer: No key is issued; the generated gcloud script creates a workload identity pool, a provider per plan and service accounts, and the required Google APIs must be enabled on the project running the script
cards.why: Defender for Cloud reaches Google Cloud through federated trust, using a workload identity pool plus impersonation of purpose-built service accounts, so no long-lived secret is stored anywhere; the script provisions the pool, per-plan providers, service accounts and project-level bindings, and APIs such as the IAM, STS, resource manager, IAM credentials and compute services must be enabled, on the management project for organization onboarding. The JSON key answer is the trap because that is how many third-party tools still work. Azure Arc matters for Defender for Servers coverage of GCP virtual machines, but it is not the connector authentication mechanism.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Defender for Cloud docs, connect a GCP project · outline 4.1

cards.q: Defender for Servers Plan 2 is on for a logistics company and agentless scanning is enabled. Every Azure VM reports vulnerability findings except four database hosts, which show nothing at all. Those four were built on ultra disk storage for write latency. The patch manager wants CVE data on them by Friday.
options: Onboard those machines through the Defender for Endpoint integration so agent-based scanning covers them
Remove the exclusion tags from the agentless scanning configuration for those machines
Raise the agentless scan frequency for the subscription so the machines are picked up sooner
Deploy a bring your own license Qualys scanner, since Defender Vulnerability Management cannot scan database servers
cards.answer: Onboard those machines through the Defender for Endpoint integration so agent-based scanning covers them
cards.why: Agentless machine scanning skips virtual machines whose disks use unsupported types, and ultra disk is on that unsupported list along with premium v2 and AKS ephemeral OS disks, so the only route to findings for those hosts is agent-based scanning through the Defender for Endpoint sensor, which Plan 1 and Plan 2 both provide. Exclusion tags are the plausible first guess, and worth checking, but they would not correlate so neatly with a single storage choice. Scan frequency is not adjustable: agentless scanning runs on a fixed daily cycle.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Enable agentless machine scanning and Configure vulnerability scanning for machines · outline 4.1

cards.q: A university's first Defender EASM discovery run returns hundreds of hosts. Among them are the web properties of an independent students' union that shares the university brand but runs its own IT, its own hosting contract and its own budget. The security team wants those hosts visible in reporting but clearly separated from what it is accountable for. Which state fits?
options: Monitor Only
Dependency
Approved Inventory
Requires Investigation
cards.answer: Monitor Only
cards.why: Monitor Only is defined for assets that are relevant to your attack surface but are neither directly controlled by you nor a technical dependency, and Microsoft gives independent franchisees and related companies as the example, which is exactly this relationship. Dependency is the closest wrong option and is reserved for third-party infrastructure that directly supports the operation of your own assets, such as a hosting provider carrying your web content. Requires Investigation is a triage state pending a decision, not the decision itself.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender EASM, What is discovery · outline 4.1

cards.q: It is 02:10. A critical attack path just lit up for an insurer: an internet-exposed web VM with an unpatched remote code execution flaw, a managed identity attached to it, and a hop from that identity to a storage account the critical asset rules tag as crown jewel patient claims data. Change control is awake and will approve one action now. Which do you take?
options: Open the path, work the remediation list and cut the entry point exposure first, breaking the path at its external node
Start with the recommendations control carrying the highest maximum secure score points
Export the path and its recommendations to the SIEM and raise a P1 for the morning team
Create an exemption for the vulnerability recommendation so the path drops off the list
cards.answer: Open the path, work the remediation list and cut the entry point exposure first, breaking the path at its external node
cards.why: Attack paths start at an external entry point and run through lateral movement to a critical target, and the remediation tab separates recommendations that mitigate the path from additional ones that only reduce exploitation risk, so removing the external reachability severs the chain immediately even before patching completes. Chasing the highest scoring control is the plausible misfire because it optimises secure score rather than this live chain, and secure score weighting is unrelated to the path in front of you. An exemption hides the finding while the route stays open, and note the path itself can take up to 24 hours to disappear after real remediation.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Identify and remediate attack paths and Critical assets protection · outline 4.1

cards.q: A hospital's public upload portal is being hammered right now with malicious document uploads. Defender for Storage caught the first wave, but the analyst sees that malware scanning on that storage account has gone quiet mid-incident: the account has already burned through its monthly scanning allowance and uploads are now landing unscanned. Blocking uploads entirely would stop clinics referring patients. What is the containment move?
options: Override the subscription-level Defender for Storage settings on that account and raise its monthly malware scanning cap
Enable sensitive data threat detection on the account so uploads are inspected again
Turn on agentless machine scanning for the subscription so the storage account is scanned
Switch the account back to the classic Defender for Storage plan, which has no scanning cap
cards.answer: Override the subscription-level Defender for Storage settings on that account and raise its monthly malware scanning cap
cards.why: Malware scanning is capped per storage account per month for cost control, defaulting to ten thousand gigabytes, and the plan supports overriding subscription-level settings for a specific account, which is exactly the lever that restores scanning without touching every other account. Enabling sensitive data threat detection is the nearest wrong answer because it is a genuine Defender for Storage feature and sounds like more inspection, but it detects exposure of sensitive data rather than scanning uploads for malware. Agentless machine scanning covers virtual machine disks, not blob uploads.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Deploy Microsoft Defender for Storage · outline 4.1

cards.q: During an active investigation into anomalous EC2 activity, an energy company's analyst finds the AWS connector in Environment settings showing an unhealthy connectivity status. Posture data for that account is stale by days. The team enabled Defender for Containers on the connector last week and changed the selected regions. What restores the feed fastest?
options: Regenerate the latest CloudFormation template from the connector and update the existing stack in AWS
Delete the connector and onboard the AWS account again as a single account
Rotate the access key held by the Defender for Cloud monitoring role in AWS IAM
Re-run the gcloud onboarding script to refresh the federated trust
cards.answer: Regenerate the latest CloudFormation template from the connector and update the existing stack in AWS
cards.why: Enabling a new Defender plan or changing plan configuration such as regions is exactly the documented trigger for refreshing the CloudFormation template, and the fix is to generate the current template and update the existing stack, keeping the stack parameters and acknowledging the IAM changes. Deleting and recreating the connector is the panic option: it discards history and configuration for a problem that a stack update solves. There is no long-lived access key to rotate, because authentication is federated with short-lived credentials, and the gcloud script belongs to GCP onboarding.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Defender for Cloud docs, connect an AWS account · outline 4.1

cards.q: A supermarket chain is containing an intrusion that began on a forgotten seasonal promotions site. The host is in nobody's configuration database and in no Defender for Cloud subscription. The incident commander needs to know within the hour whether the same forgotten estate holds more of these. What do you do with Defender EASM?
options: Search the inventory for the compromised host and pivot on its shared certificate, name server and address block relationships to surface sibling assets
Add the compromised host as an exclusion in the relevant discovery group so it stops skewing the inventory
Create a discovery group seeded only with that host and set its recurrence to Never
Wait for the weekly scheduled discovery run to refresh the attack surface with the new information
cards.answer: Search the inventory for the compromised host and pivot on its shared certificate, name server and address block relationships to surface sibling assets
cards.why: Discovery works by recursing outward from known assets through Whois records, DNS records, shared certificates and address block or ASN relationships, so an already indexed compromised host is itself a lead into the rest of the unmanaged estate that was built alongside it. Adding an exclusion is the actively harmful option: exclusions keep entities out of inventory, which is the opposite of what an investigation needs. Seeding a one-off group with a single host narrows the aperture, and waiting for the weekly cadence spends the hour you do not have.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender EASM, What is discovery and Use and manage Defender EASM discovery · outline 4.1

cards.q: The post-incident review at a car parts manufacturer establishes that the exploited CVE had been present for months but never appeared in the vulnerability findings list. Someone had created a rule years ago suppressing findings below a chosen scoring threshold, and the CVE fell just under it. The team wants suppression to stay possible but auditable and current. What should they put in place?
options: Retire the disable rules and manage exceptions through exemptions instead, since disable rules are being deprecated
Keep the disable rules but raise the minimum severity setting from medium to high
Add exclusion tags to the agentless scanning configuration for the affected machines
Configure continuous export of vulnerability findings so suppressed items still reach the SIEM
cards.answer: Retire the disable rules and manage exceptions through exemptions instead, since disable rules are being deprecated
cards.why: Disabled findings are invisible and do not affect secure score, which is precisely how a CVE hides for months; Microsoft is deprecating disable rules as part of the move to individual recommendations and directs teams to exemptions, which carry the exception explicitly. Raising the minimum severity is the tempting half-measure because it narrows the blast radius, but it leaves the same silent suppression mechanism in place. Exclusion tags stop machines being scanned at all, which is a wider hole, not a narrower one.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Disable vulnerability findings and Exclude machines from agentless scanning · outline 4.1

cards.q: A university's quarterly posture review finds the same twelve high risk recommendations open as last quarter. Each belongs to a different faculty resource owner, none of whom reads the security team's spreadsheet, and nobody has a deadline. Defender CSPM is licensed and enabled. What should have been in place, and should be now?
options: Governance rules that assign each recommendation to its resource owner with a remediation timeframe and tracked progress
Workflow automation triggering a Logic App to email the security team when a recommendation changes state
Continuous export of recommendations to a Log Analytics workspace with a weekly compliance snapshot
Enforce and deny on the underlying policies so noncompliant resources cannot be created
cards.answer: Governance rules that assign each recommendation to its resource owner with a remediation timeframe and tracked progress
cards.why: Governance is the Defender CSPM capability built for exactly this failure mode: it drives remediation at scale by assigning owners and due dates and tracking whether the estate is converging on the security policy. Enforce and deny is the strong nearby answer and belongs in the hardening plan, but it prevents future noncompliant resources rather than closing the twelve findings already sitting there with no owner. Workflow automation and continuous export move information around; neither creates accountability or a deadline.
cards.citation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, What is Cloud Security Posture Management and Drive remediation with governance rules · outline 4.1

cards.q: A grocery retailer already runs Microsoft Sentinel in the Defender portal on its head-office workspace, which is the primary. It now onboards a second workspace belonging to the recently acquired logistics arm, and the logistics SOC keeps its own analysts. After onboarding, the logistics team complains that Defender XDR incidents never appear in their workspace queue. What should you tell them?
options: Defender XDR alerts and incidents sync only to the primary workspace, so a secondary workspace shows only its own incidents, although it can still ingest Defender table data
A second Defender XDR data connector must be enabled on the logistics workspace so that XDR incidents are duplicated into both queues
The logistics workspace needs the Microsoft Sentinel Contributor role assigned at tenant scope before XDR incidents will replicate to it
Multiple workspaces in the Defender portal are only supported through Azure Lighthouse delegation, so the logistics workspace must be delegated first
cards.answer: Defender XDR alerts and incidents sync only to the primary workspace, so a secondary workspace shows only its own incidents, although it can still ingest Defender table data
cards.why: The Defender portal supports one primary workspace plus any number of secondary ones, and the Defender XDR connector attaches to the primary workspace alone. Incident creation and alert correlation stay separated per workspace. The nearest wrong answer is enabling a second XDR connector: any standalone Microsoft connectors on secondary workspaces are deliberately disconnected at onboarding precisely to stop tenant-based alerts being counted twice, so that path is blocked by design rather than merely inadvisable.
cards.citation: Defender portal support for multiple Sentinel workspaces (workspaces-defender-portal) · outline 4.2

cards.q: A regional teaching hospital hires a detection engineer who must install the Windows Forwarded Events solution, keep it updated, and build analytics rules on top of it. She already has Microsoft Sentinel Responder on the resource group holding the workspace, and every install attempt in the content hub fails. Which single change gives her exactly what she needs?
options: Assign Microsoft Sentinel Contributor at the resource group that holds the workspace
Assign Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator at the resource group that holds the workspace
Assign Log Analytics Reader on the workspace so she can read the table schemas the solution creates
Assign the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role at tenant scope
cards.answer: Assign Microsoft Sentinel Contributor at the resource group that holds the workspace
cards.why: Installing, updating, and removing content hub items requires Microsoft Sentinel Contributor at resource group level, and that role also carries the create and edit rights for analytics rules she needs. The closest wrong choice is Playbook Operator: it only lets someone list, view, and manually run playbooks, and it grants nothing at all in the content hub. Responder alone stops at managing incidents.
cards.citation: Microsoft Sentinel roles and permissions (roles) and out-of-the-box content management (sentinel-solutions-deploy) · outline 4.2

cards.q: An engineer at a car parts manufacturer installs the content hub solution for the plant firewall so its logs reach Sentinel. The solution installs cleanly, but when he opens Data connectors there is no connector he can point at the Linux collector VM sitting in the plant DMZ. What did he most likely skip?
options: He installed the solution on its own instead of choosing Install with dependencies, so the Common Event Format solution carrying the CEF via AMA connector never came with it
He installed from the card view rather than the list view, which omits data connectors from the deployment
He needed to create the destination table before installing, because connector pages stay hidden until their table exists
He should have registered the collector VM in Microsoft Defender for Cloud first, because unregistered machines hide their connectors
cards.answer: He installed the solution on its own instead of choosing Install with dependencies, so the Common Event Format solution carrying the CEF via AMA connector never came with it
cards.why: Vendor solutions that ride on the unified Azure Monitor Agent connectors for CEF, Syslog, or custom logs declare dependencies, and Install with dependencies pulls in the solution that actually carries the connector. The tempting wrong answer is the pre-created table: that requirement belongs to Custom Logs via AMA, where you build the table ending in _CL yourself, not to CEF collection, which lands in the built-in CommonSecurityLog table.
cards.citation: Sentinel solution content, installing with dependencies (sentinel-solutions-deploy) · outline 4.2

cards.q: A retail bank wants control-plane activity from roughly four hundred existing Azure resources across two subscriptions flowing into Sentinel, and it wants any resource created next quarter covered automatically. An engineer opens the Azure Activity connector page and starts the Azure Policy assignment wizard. Which step makes sure the four hundred resources that already exist start reporting?
options: On the Remediation tab of the policy assignment, select the option to create a remediation task
On the Parameters tab, clear the check box that hides parameters which do not require input
Add a diagnostic setting by hand on each subscription after the policy assignment finishes
Raise the workspace analytics retention above thirty days so historical activity is backfilled
cards.answer: On the Remediation tab of the policy assignment, select the option to create a remediation task
cards.why: A policy assignment governs resources created from that point on; a remediation task is what reaches back and applies the diagnostic setting to resources that already exist. The nearest wrong option, clearing the parameter filter, is a real step in the same wizard but only exposes the workspace and log-type parameters, and does nothing about existing scope. Retention changes never backfill data that was never ingested.
cards.citation: Sentinel diagnostic settings-based connectors (connect-services-diagnostic-setting-based) · outline 4.2

cards.q: A university SOC collects both plain syslog from Linux research hosts and CEF from its perimeter appliances through one Linux forwarder. Billing shows the same appliance events landing in CommonSecurityLog and in Syslog, doubling cost. The appliance vendor gives no way to change the facility it writes to. What is the correct fix?
options: Add an ingestion-time transformation to the data collection rule that drops CEF-looking records from the syslog stream
Move the CEF appliances onto a second forwarder VM so each format has its own listener
Switch the syslog daemon on the forwarder from rsyslog to syslog-ng, which separates the two formats natively
Change the CEF data collection rule to send to the Microsoft-Syslog stream so only one table is written
cards.answer: Add an ingestion-time transformation to the data collection rule that drops CEF-looking records from the syslog stream
cards.why: When the source cannot be moved to a different facility, the documented remedy is a KQL transformation on the DCR that filters CEF messages out of the syslog stream, checking both the process name and the message body because some vendors do not honour the RFC header format. The closest wrong answer, a second forwarder, splits the machines but not the facility, so the same facility still feeds both streams and the duplication survives. Repointing CEF at Microsoft-Syslog would simply destroy the CommonSecurityLog parsing.
cards.citation: Syslog and CEF via AMA connectors, avoiding duplicate ingestion (cef-syslog-ama-overview) · outline 4.2

cards.q: An insurer runs 900 Arc-enabled Windows servers. The security lead wants breach-relevant signals such as sign-ins and process creation, and is willing to lose sign-out records to hold volume down. Which choice in the Windows Security Events data collection rule matches that intent with the least engineering?
options: Select the prebuilt Minimal event set
Select the prebuilt Common event set
Select All events and add a workspace transformation that drops event ID 4634
Select Custom and paste an XPath expression that names each event ID individually
cards.answer: Select the prebuilt Minimal event set
cards.why: Minimal is defined as the small breach-indicative set: it keeps successful and failed logons and process creation while deliberately omitting sign-out, which is high volume and of little detection value. The nearest wrong choice is Common, which exists to keep a full audit trail including 4634, so it holds precisely the records the lead agreed to give up. Custom XPath would reach the same place but is unnecessary work when a prebuilt set already expresses the requirement.
cards.citation: Windows security event set reference for Sentinel collection (windows-security-event-id-reference) · outline 4.2

cards.q: A defence supplier keeps most Windows member servers off the internet and funnels their events to two hardened collector servers instead. The SOC wants those forwarded events in Sentinel via the Windows Forwarded Events connector. What must be true before the connector will produce data?
options: Windows Event Collection is running on the collector servers and the Azure Monitor Agent is installed on those collector machines
The Azure Monitor Agent is installed on every source server, with the collectors acting only as a network relay
The collectors run the Linux log forwarder installation script so the syslog daemon listens on port 514
A custom table ending in _CL is created first, because forwarded events have no built-in schema
cards.answer: Windows Event Collection is running on the collector servers and the Azure Monitor Agent is installed on those collector machines
cards.why: Windows Event Forwarding concentrates events on a collector, so the agent belongs on the collector, and the connector prerequisite is exactly that: WEC enabled and running with the agent on that machine. Installing the agent on every source, the closest wrong option, defeats the whole reason the estate was designed this way and is not what the connector expects. The forwarder script and the _CL table belong to Linux syslog and text-file collection respectively.
cards.citation: Connect Microsoft Sentinel with a Windows agent-based data connector (connect-services-windows-based) · outline 4.2

cards.q: A logistics firm runs a warehouse access-control appliance that writes flat text logs and cannot host an agent, so it ships lines to a Linux forwarder. An engineer prepares the destination table in the workspace before configuring Custom Logs via AMA. How should that table be built?
options: A table whose name ends in _CL with two columns, TimeGenerated and Message, because the records arrive through a forwarder
A table whose name ends in _CL with two columns, TimeGenerated and RawData, regardless of how the records arrive
A table whose name ends in _SRCH with TimeGenerated and RawData, because search job tables accept arbitrary text
No table is needed, because the data collection rule creates one automatically from the first parsed record
cards.answer: A table whose name ends in _CL with two columns, TimeGenerated and Message, because the records arrive through a forwarder
cards.why: The destination table must carry the _CL suffix and just two columns, a datetime and the whole log line. The line column is called RawData when collection happens on the machine hosting the application, and Message when a log forwarder sits in between, which is the case here and is why the paired transformation renames the field. The RawData variant is the near miss: correct shape, wrong field name for this topology. The _SRCH suffix belongs to tables produced by search jobs.
cards.citation: Azure Monitor Agent text-log collection (connect-custom-logs-ama) · outline 4.2

cards.q: An energy utility moves its containment playbooks into a new resource group for change-control reasons. A SOC engineer builds an automation rule to run one of them on incident creation, but in the run playbook picker the moved playbooks appear greyed out. What resolves this?
options: Grant the Microsoft Sentinel service account explicit permissions on the resource group holding the playbooks, which needs Owner rights on that group
Give the engineer the Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator role on the new resource group
Give the engineer Logic App Contributor on the new resource group so the playbooks become selectable
Recreate the automation rule with the alert trigger, because incident-trigger rules cannot call playbooks across resource groups
cards.answer: Grant the Microsoft Sentinel service account explicit permissions on the resource group holding the playbooks, which needs Owner rights on that group
cards.why: Automation rules run playbooks under a dedicated Sentinel service account, not under the author, and that account must be granted rights on the resource group where the playbook lives; the Manage playbook permissions link does this and asks for Owner on the group. The nearest wrong answer, Playbook Operator for the engineer, only enables that person to run a playbook by hand, which does nothing for unattended execution. Trigger type is irrelevant here; both trigger families can call playbooks of the matching type.
cards.citation: Automate threat response with automation rules, permissions for automation rules to run playbooks (automate-incident-handling-with-automation-rules) · outline 4.2

cards.q: A payments processor must keep firewall records for seven years to satisfy its regulator, but its hunters only ever query the last three months interactively. A table currently sits in the Analytics tier at 180 days analytics retention with total retention also at 180 days. Which change meets both needs at the lowest cost?
options: Lower analytics retention to 90 days and raise total retention to seven years
Leave analytics retention at 180 days and raise total retention to seven years
Move the table to the Data Lake tier and set its retention to seven years
Keep the settings and run a monthly search job that copies older records into a new table
cards.answer: Lower analytics retention to 90 days and raise total retention to seven years
cards.why: Analytics retention is the expensive hot window and 90 days covers the hunters, while total retention carries the same table onward in the lake for up to twelve years at low cost, which satisfies the regulator. Moving the whole table to the Data Lake tier is the tempting alternative but it stops real-time analytics rules, alerting, and hunting on that table entirely, so the three-month working window disappears. Leaving 180 days hot simply pays twice as much for a window nobody uses.
cards.citation: Sentinel data tiers and retention management (manage-data-overview), log retention plans (log-plans) · outline 4.2

cards.q: Right now, at 02:40, a hospital is watching an operator account move between domain controllers. The DCR for Windows Security Events was set to the Minimal event set, so the analysts can see logons but have no sign-out or special-privilege assignment records to bound the sessions. The attacker is still active. What is the containment move that restores the missing visibility fastest?
options: Edit the existing data collection rule to Custom and add XPath expressions for the Security channel event IDs the team is missing
Create a second data collection rule targeting the same domain controllers with the All events option
Raise analytics retention on the SecurityEvent table so the absent event IDs become queryable
Run a search job over the SecurityEvent table for the past 24 hours to recover the sign-out records
cards.answer: Edit the existing data collection rule to Custom and add XPath expressions for the Security channel event IDs the team is missing
cards.why: Events not selected by the rule were never sent, so the only way forward is to widen what the agent collects, and editing the rule in place applies to every associated machine without a second association to manage. Standing up a second rule with All events is the close alternative: it works, but it floods the workspace with the full unfiltered Security and AppLocker channels mid-incident and leaves a rule to unpick afterwards. Retention and search jobs only reach data that was already ingested, and these records never were.
cards.citation: Collect Windows events with Azure Monitor Agent, XPath filtering (data-collection-windows-events) and Windows security event sets (windows-security-event-id-reference) · outline 4.2

cards.q: A commercial bank is in the middle of a credential-stuffing wave. The automation rule that should tag, assign, and then call the IP-blocking playbook is firing, the tag and the assignment land, but the playbook action never executes and the source addresses keep hitting. The playbook itself runs fine when tested from the Logic Apps designer. What do you do to get blocking working in this incident?
options: Open Manage playbook permissions and grant Sentinel rights on the playbook resource group, then let the rule act on the next incident update
Raise the automation rule order number so its playbook action is evaluated ahead of the other rules in the queue
Change the automation rule trigger from incident created to alert created so it fires on every alert
Rebuild the playbook on the Logic Apps Standard plan, because Consumption playbooks cannot be called from automation rules
cards.answer: Open Manage playbook permissions and grant Sentinel rights on the playbook resource group, then let the rule act on the next incident update
cards.why: Non-playbook actions such as tagging and assignment run natively, so a rule that performs those but silently skips the playbook points squarely at the Sentinel service account lacking rights on the playbook resource group. Reordering, the nearest wrong answer, changes which rule runs first but never grants the missing permission, so the action would still be skipped. Both Logic Apps plans are supported from automation rules, and switching to the alert trigger would abandon the incident-shaped conditions the rule depends on.
cards.citation: Automate threat response with automation rules, actions and playbook permissions (automate-incident-handling-with-automation-rules) · outline 4.2

cards.q: An online retailer is dealing with a live intrusion. Overnight a cost-cutting change moved the CommonSecurityLog table to the Data Lake tier, and since then every firewall analytics rule has stopped producing alerts. The team needs detections back and also needs to read last night's perimeter traffic immediately. What do you do?
options: Set the table back to the Analytics tier so new records feed the rules again, and query last night's records with a KQL job against the lake in the meantime
Leave the table in the Data Lake tier and rewrite the affected analytics rules to query the lake directly
Restore the table from long-term retention, which returns both the historical records and the rule coverage
Raise total retention on the table, because analytics rules resume once total retention exceeds analytics retention
cards.answer: Set the table back to the Analytics tier so new records feed the rules again, and query last night's records with a KQL job against the lake in the meantime
cards.why: Data Lake tier data is deliberately outside real-time features, so alerting, analytics rules, and hunting stop the moment a table is moved there, and the tier must be changed back for detections to resume on incoming data. The lake is still readable through KQL jobs and notebooks, which is how the overnight window gets examined without waiting. Rewriting the rules against the lake, the nearest wrong answer, is not possible in the way it sounds because scheduled analytics rules are among the features the lake tier does not support.
cards.citation: Manage data tiers and retention, what happens when you modify table settings (manage-data-overview) · outline 4.2

cards.q: A chemicals manufacturer discovers, mid-incident, that a custom detection rule was quietly edited and two device indicators were removed from Defender XDR earlier this week. Nobody on the SOC admits to it, and the attacker may still hold an administrative session. Where do you go right now to establish who performed those administrative actions and when?
options: The Audit page in the Defender portal, searching the unified audit log for the Defender XDR administrative activities in that date range
The SentinelHealth table, filtering for data fetch status change events over the same period
The CloudAuditEvents table in advanced hunting, filtering by operation name
The SecurityAlert table, correlating alerts raised by the custom detection rule before it changed
cards.answer: The Audit page in the Defender portal, searching the unified audit log for the Defender XDR administrative activities in that date range
cards.why: Defender XDR administrative actions, including creating or editing custom detection rules and creating or removing indicators of compromise, are audited automatically into Microsoft Purview Audit and are searchable from the Audit page in the Defender portal by activity, date, and user. CloudAuditEvents is the closest-looking distractor but it holds cloud platform control-plane records surfaced by Defender for Cloud, not portal administration of Defender XDR, and it returns nothing at all if Defender for Cloud is not in play. SentinelHealth reports connector health, not who changed what.
cards.citation: Defender XDR audit log search (microsoft-xdr-auditing) and CloudAuditEvents table reference · outline 4.2

cards.q: After a breach at an airline that went unseen for eleven days, the review finds the cause was a third-party connector that had stopped delivering weeks earlier with nobody noticing. The SOC lead wants a control that would page someone the next time a feed goes quiet. What should be put in place?
options: Turn on health monitoring so the SentinelHealth table is populated, then build an Azure Monitor alert rule on a query that finds connectors flipping from success to failure
Rely on the Table insights view in the Defender portal and its Last data received column as the alerting mechanism
Add an automation rule with the incident update trigger that notifies the team when no incidents arrive from that connector
Shorten analytics retention on the affected tables so that gaps in ingestion become visible sooner in queries
cards.answer: Turn on health monitoring so the SentinelHealth table is populated, then build an Azure Monitor alert rule on a query that finds connectors flipping from success to failure
cards.why: SentinelHealth only exists once health monitoring is enabled, and Microsoft's guidance is to alert on health drift with Azure Monitor alert rules rather than analytics rules, which is what turns a silent feed into a page. Table insights is the seductive wrong answer because its Last data received and fluctuation cards do surface exactly this symptom, but the documentation is explicit that it is a visualization surface, not an alerting one, and tables below a megabyte a day are not even evaluated. Automation rules react to incidents, so they cannot fire on the absence of data.
cards.citation: Monitor the health of your data connectors (monitor-data-connector-health) and Configure table settings, Table insights limitations (manage-table-tiers-retention) · outline 4.2

cards.q: A university is rebuilding its collection design after an audit. The network operations team, who are not part of the SOC, need to read syslog from the appliances they own, and nothing else in the workspace. The syslog reaches Sentinel through one shared Linux forwarder for the whole campus. What should the design have included?
options: A separate log forwarder per owning team, plus resource-context RBAC granting each team log reader rights on the resources their forwarder represents
The Microsoft Sentinel Reader role for the network team, scoped to the resource group that contains the workspace
A second Log Analytics workspace for network operations, with cross-workspace queries joining it to the SOC workspace
A workspace transformation that strips the appliance records the network team is not entitled to see
cards.answer: A separate log forwarder per owning team, plus resource-context RBAC granting each team log reader rights on the resources their forwarder represents
cards.why: Syslog and CEF records are not Azure resources, so they inherit the resource ID of the forwarding VM, which means one shared forwarder makes every team's events indistinguishable for access purposes; separate forwarders per team, each with a resource ID, is the documented way to make resource-context RBAC work here. Sentinel Reader is the closest wrong answer and fails the requirement in the opposite direction, since it opens the whole workspace and the Sentinel experience rather than a slice of it. A second workspace would solve the permission problem but is heavy, and cross-workspace querying would reintroduce the exposure.
cards.citation: Resource-context RBAC for Sentinel data, resource IDs with log forwarding (resource-context-rbac) · outline 4.2

cards.q: A regional grocery chain runs Microsoft 365 E3 with Defender for Endpoint, and the SOC lead wants a Security Copilot workspace stood up this week for a pilot with six analysts. She opens securitycopilot.microsoft.com, is offered a Get started flow, and asks you what actually has to be in place before that flow will complete. What do you tell her?
options: An Azure subscription with Contributor or Owner rights on the target resource group, plus Security Administrator or higher in the tenant, because the pilot must provision at least one Security Compute Unit
Nothing beyond her Global Reader role, because the workspace provisions automatically for any tenant with a Defender for Endpoint licence
An upgrade to Microsoft 365 E5 first, because Security Copilot cannot be provisioned manually on any lower licence
A Microsoft Sentinel Log Analytics workspace in the same region, because Security Copilot capacity is attached to a Sentinel workspace
cards.answer: An Azure subscription with Contributor or Owner rights on the target resource group, plus Security Administrator or higher in the tenant, because the pilot must provision at least one Security Compute Unit
cards.why: A non-E5 and non-E7 tenant follows manual onboarding: it names a workspace, then provisions SCU capacity against an Azure subscription and resource group, which needs Azure Contributor or Owner on that resource group and Security Administrator or higher in the tenant. The nearest wrong answer is the E5 upgrade, which is a real path to inclusion capacity but not a prerequisite, since manual provisioning exists precisely so lower-licensed tenants can buy SCUs starting at one unit.
cards.citation: Microsoft Learn: manual onboarding for tenants without an E5 or E7 licence · outline 4.3

cards.q: A teaching hospital provisioned three SCUs and left overage at zero. On a quiet Tuesday the night analyst burns all three units on a long promptbook at 02:20, and by 02:35 Copilot refuses further prompts. He messages you asking whether the units he did not use earlier in the evening will carry him through. What is the accurate answer about how provisioned capacity behaves?
options: Provisioned SCUs refresh on fixed clock-hour blocks and unused units expire at the end of the hour rather than rolling over, so his earlier idle hours bank nothing
Provisioned SCUs accumulate across the billing day and are only zeroed at midnight in the tenant home geo
Provisioned SCUs refresh on a rolling sixty-minute window measured from each session start, so capacity returns sixty minutes after his promptbook began
Provisioned SCUs are pooled monthly, so unused night-time units offset heavy daytime use across the whole billing period
cards.answer: Provisioned SCUs refresh on fixed clock-hour blocks and unused units expire at the end of the hour rather than rolling over, so his earlier idle hours bank nothing
cards.why: Provisioned capacity grants the full unit count each clock hour, for example 02:00 to 03:00, and anything unused simply lapses when that hour ends. The rolling-window option is the trap because it sounds like the same idea, but a rolling sixty minutes from session start would let a heavy user shift capacity around, and Microsoft explicitly documents fixed hour blocks rather than rolling ones.
cards.citation: Microsoft Learn: Security Compute Units and capacity models · outline 4.3

cards.q: A car parts manufacturer is trying to trim Security Copilot spend. Their platform engineer provisions one SCU at 09:05, tears it down at 09:35 when a hunt finishes, then provisions another at 09:45 for a second hunt, and is surprised the 09:00 hour shows two units billed. What guidance stops this happening again?
options: Make provisioning changes at the start of the hour, because provisioned capacity is billed in hourly blocks with a one hour minimum regardless of when within the hour the change happens
Switch the capacity to overage only, because overage capacity is exempt from hourly billing and is invoiced monthly in arrears
Move the capacity resource to a cheaper Azure region, because SCU block billing is priced per region and re-provisioning is free outside the home geo
Delete and recreate the workspace between hunts, because billing follows the workspace rather than the capacity resource
cards.answer: Make provisioning changes at the start of the hour, because provisioned capacity is billed in hourly blocks with a one hour minimum regardless of when within the hour the change happens
cards.why: Provisioned capacity bills in whole hourly blocks with a one hour minimum, so two separate provisions inside the 09:00 hour are two billed units, and the documented advice is to change unit counts at the top of the hour. The overage answer is the closest miss: overage really is consumption-based and billed to one decimal place, but it does not exempt anything from hourly provisioned billing, and it is added on top of provisioned units rather than replacing them.
cards.citation: Microsoft Learn: Security Compute Units and capacity models, billing section · outline 4.3

cards.q: A retail bank assigns a new tier-two analyst the Copilot contributor role. She can sign in, open a session and get answers about public threat intelligence, but every prompt asking Copilot to summarise incidents in the bank's Microsoft Sentinel workspace comes back with nothing useful. Her manager insists the role assignment is correct. What is the fix?
options: Grant her an Azure RBAC role on the Sentinel workspace such as Microsoft Sentinel Reader, because Copilot roles gate the platform while the underlying service RBAC still gates the data
Promote her to Copilot owner, because only owners can invoke plugins that read from Azure-hosted security data
Add her to the Everyone group in Security Copilot role assignment, which restores the default data access bundle
Have an owner turn on the Microsoft Sentinel plugin at tenant scope, because plugin availability rather than RBAC controls what data a prompt can reach
cards.answer: Grant her an Azure RBAC role on the Sentinel workspace such as Microsoft Sentinel Reader, because Copilot roles gate the platform while the underlying service RBAC still gates the data
cards.why: Copilot owner and contributor are platform roles that grant no access to security data on their own; Copilot uses on-behalf-of authentication, so it never exceeds the user's own service permissions. The plugin option is the strongest distractor because a restricted plugin genuinely can block a workload, but here she reaches other plugins fine, and turning a plugin on for the tenant would still leave her without any Azure role on the Sentinel workspace.
cards.citation: Understand authentication in Microsoft Security Copilot, Access the capabilities of Microsoft plugins · outline 4.3

cards.q: A university inherited a Security Copilot tenant where the Everyone group holds Copilot contributor. Students in research groups now see a Copilot experience with no data behind it, and internal audit wants access narrowed. The identity team asks what a safe migration looks like before they touch anything. What do you advise?
options: Remove the Everyone group and assign the Recommended Microsoft Security roles group instead, understanding that Everyone cannot be assigned again once removed
Leave Everyone in place and layer a deny assignment on the student groups, because Copilot role assignment supports deny entries
Convert Everyone into a dynamic membership group filtered to staff, because Copilot evaluates dynamic rules at prompt time
Assign every analyst the Security Administrator Entra role individually, which supersedes the Everyone group assignment
cards.answer: Remove the Everyone group and assign the Recommended Microsoft Security roles group instead, understanding that Everyone cannot be assigned again once removed
cards.why: The recommended bundle gives platform access to people who already hold Microsoft security roles, and the documented catch is that removing Everyone is one-way, so the replacement must be planned before the removal. The Security Administrator option is the tempting one because that role does inherit Copilot owner, but Microsoft explicitly warns against handing out a highly privileged Entra role purely to obtain Copilot access; use a security group added to a Copilot role instead.
cards.citation: Understand authentication in Microsoft Security Copilot, Recommended Security Copilot contributor roles · outline 4.3

cards.q: A mid-market insurer outsources night cover to an MSSP. The MSSP wants its analysts to prompt against the insurer's Microsoft Sentinel workspaces from the MSSP's own tenant using Azure Lighthouse delegation. The insurer's finance lead wants to know whose Security Compute Units pay for those prompts. What is correct?
options: Under Azure Lighthouse the partner tenant's capacity plan is consumed, whereas GDAP and B2B guest access both consume the customer tenant's capacity plan
Under Azure Lighthouse the customer tenant's capacity plan is consumed, because the data being queried lives in the customer subscription
All three partner access models consume the partner tenant's capacity plan, since the prompt is issued from the partner portal
Lighthouse prompts consume no SCUs at all, because delegated resource management is billed through the Azure Consumption Commitment rather than Copilot capacity
cards.answer: Under Azure Lighthouse the partner tenant's capacity plan is consumed, whereas GDAP and B2B guest access both consume the customer tenant's capacity plan
cards.why: Lighthouse is the outlier of the three partner models: the analyst works from the partner tenant against delegated Azure resources, so the partner's SCUs are drawn down, while GDAP and B2B guest sign-in both bill the customer's capacity. The mirror-image option is the natural guess because data residency intuition says the data owner pays, but Microsoft's comparison table puts Lighthouse consumption in the partner tenant. Lighthouse also supports only the Sentinel and NL2KQL Sentinel plugins.
cards.citation: Grant partners access to Microsoft Security Copilot, Compare access methods · outline 4.3

cards.q: A logistics firm's Copilot owner restricts preinstalled plugin availability to Owners only while an internal review runs. Within an hour the tier-one queue complains that incident summaries and guided response have vanished from the Defender portal sidecar. The owner insists she only changed a standalone setting. What is the accurate account of what happened, and what happens to plugins added later?
options: Plugin restrictions apply to both standalone and embedded experiences, and any newly released preinstalled plugin defaults to Owners only until she configures it otherwise
Plugin restrictions apply only to the standalone portal, so the Defender symptoms must come from a separate Defender XDR role change
Plugin restrictions apply to embedded experiences only after a tenant-wide restart, and new preinstalled plugins default to All users
Plugin restrictions apply to custom plugins only, so preinstalled Microsoft plugins such as Defender XDR are unaffected by the toggle
cards.answer: Plugin restrictions apply to both standalone and embedded experiences, and any newly released preinstalled plugin defaults to Owners only until she configures it otherwise
cards.why: Restricting preinstalled plugin availability is an immediate tenant-wide change covering the embedded Copilot surfaces such as Defender XDR, which is why Microsoft warns owners to notify users first, and once restriction is on, subsequent preinstalled plugins arrive Owners only. The standalone-only option is the seductive one because the setting lives in the standalone portal's plugin settings page, but the blast radius is explicitly both experiences.
cards.citation: Manage plugins in Microsoft Security Copilot, Manage preinstalled plugins · outline 4.3

cards.q: A national pharmacy chain wants its two senior detection engineers, who hold Copilot contributor, to be able to build and test their own OpenAI-schema plugins for a vendor reputation service, but nothing they build should reach the wider SOC without owner sign-off. Which owner configuration delivers exactly that?
options: Set the personal-scope permission (who may add and manage plugins for themselves) to Owners and Contributors, and leave the workspace-scope permission (who may publish plugins to everyone) at Owners only
Set both custom plugin permissions to Owners and Contributors, then rely on the private tag applied at upload time to keep the plugin scoped to the uploader
Leave both permissions at Owners only and have the engineers upload through the Security Store publishing flow instead
Set the workspace-scope permission (who may publish plugins to everyone) to Owners and Contributors, and leave personal custom plugins at Owners only
cards.answer: Set the personal-scope permission (who may add and manage plugins for themselves) to Owners and Contributors, and leave the workspace-scope permission (who may publish plugins to everyone) at Owners only
cards.why: The two settings are layered: the first governs user-scope plugins and must be opened to contributors before the tenant-scope question is even active, and leaving the second at Owners only keeps publishing under owner control. The both-open option fails because although the upload dialog does offer a private choice, the contributors would then also be permitted to choose organisation-wide scope, which is exactly the sign-off gate the chain wants to keep.
cards.citation: Manage plugins in Microsoft Security Copilot, Options for managing plugins · outline 4.3

cards.q: A utilities SOC buys a partner-built triage agent that reads Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Defender data. The Copilot owner opens the agent page and finds the Set up button greyed out behind a banner about required consent. She has Copilot owner and Security Administrator. What unblocks the deployment?
options: A Microsoft Entra Global Administrator must approve the agent's required permissions, after which the Copilot owner or a contributor completes identity, trigger and parameter setup
She must raise her own account to Copilot owner in a second workspace, because partner agents are approved per workspace rather than per tenant
She must first buy the agent again through the Azure Marketplace, because Security Store purchases do not carry consent for Microsoft data access
She must create a Microsoft Entra Agent ID for the partner agent, because partner agents cannot run under an existing user account
cards.answer: A Microsoft Entra Global Administrator must approve the agent's required permissions, after which the Copilot owner or a contributor completes identity, trigger and parameter setup
cards.why: When a partner-built agent reaches a Microsoft tool and Microsoft product data such as Intune, Entra, Sentinel or Defender, a Global Administrator has to grant that consent, and the owner's own flow offers a Copy link to hand to them. The Agent ID option is the closest miss and is backwards: creating a dedicated agent identity is currently offered for Microsoft-built agents, while partner-built agent setup assigns an existing user account.
cards.citation: Setup and Manage Security Copilot agents, Set up partner-built agents · outline 4.3

cards.q: A hotel group trialled a partner agent from Security Store for a quarter, decided against it, and removed it from the Agents page in Security Copilot. Two months later procurement is still seeing a charge for it and asks the SOC why. What is the correct explanation and remedy?
options: Removing an agent from Security Copilot does not end the Security Store subscription, so billing must be managed in Security Store, separately from the SCU consumption the agent used while running
Removing an agent leaves a thirty day grace period on the Copilot capacity, after which the charge stops automatically with no action needed
The residual charge is SCU overage the agent accrued after removal, and the fix is to lower the overage limit on the capacity resource
Agent subscriptions are cancelled from the Copilot owner settings page under capacity management, which is where Security Store purchases are terminated
cards.answer: Removing an agent from Security Copilot does not end the Security Store subscription, so billing must be managed in Security Store, separately from the SCU consumption the agent used while running
cards.why: Security Store keeps purchasing and billing deliberately separate from operational management in Security Copilot, so uninstalling the agent stops it running but leaves the subscription alive until cancelled in the Store. The owner settings answer is the plausible trap because capacity management does live there, but that page governs SCU association and units, not partner subscription billing.
cards.citation: Microsoft Security Store in Microsoft Security Copilot, Discover and get agents · outline 4.3

cards.q: It is 03:12 and a payments processor is containing an active ransomware deployment. The incident commander's prompts now return an error saying Copilot cannot respond because of high usage in the organisation, and the embedded Defender sidecar has gone quiet too. Provisioned SCUs and the overage limit are both fully consumed. What is the containment move right now?
options: Get the Azure capacity owner or contributor to raise provisioned SCUs or the overage limit immediately, expecting the adjustment to take effect within about thirty minutes
Have every analyst close the embedded Copilot sidecar in Defender to stop it consuming units while the incident runs
Delete the capacity resource and recreate it larger, because a fresh capacity starts with an empty consumption counter
Switch the prompt evaluation location to another geography, which routes the session to a different capacity pool
